title: The assistant offers a 20 percent promo code that does not exist
scenario: Kestrel's assistant tells customers that code SPRING20 takes 20 percent off a tent. Checkout rejects it, stores are honoring the price, and the grounding check that should block invented promotions logged grounded=True. The product team blames the model upgrade from the same weekend.
task: Trace the code to its source in the tool results the model saw
Explain why the grounding check passed it and why a legitimate discount was blocked
Rule the model upgrade in or out from the timeline
Ground only on trusted structured fields and fence review text in the prompt
acceptance: Injected codes and review prices are blocked; legitimate discounts are shown
Prices and promotions must belong to the cited products
Reviews cannot escape the untrusted fence
Root cause named with evidence; red herring ruled out
